title: eval-harness: integrate quality metrics and CI hook for prompt-set regression gating
author: Aditi Chandra
release_notes: Adds CI gating for eval-harness prompt-set regressions and integrates new quality metrics (embedding-similarity thresholds and aggregated quality scores) into nightly and PR-level runs. Enables automatic failure of PRs that degrade prompt-set quality beyond tolerated thresholds.
description:
Motivation: Our nightly evals catch regressions, but PR-level feedback is slow and noisy. This change integrates a small set of lightweight quality metrics into the eval-harness and exposes a GitHub Action CI hook that runs prompt-set checks on PRs. The goal is to provide fast, actionable feedback for changes that can degrade prompt quality (generation drift, format regressions) without running the full nightly suite.

Summary:
- Add two new metric collectors to eval-harness: embedding-similarity (centroid cosine) and token-pattern coverage (structural checks).
- Implement an aggregated quality_score and configuration-driven thresholds per prompt-set.
- Add a GitHub Action (ci/eval-prompt-gate.yml) that runs the lightweight checks on changed prompts and model-serving code paths.
- Wire CI to post a single aggregated comment with metric breakdown and pass/fail status; when the gate fails CI marks the PR as failed.
- Update docs and add a migration note for teams that rely on the previous nightly-only alerts.

Checklist:
- [x] Metric implementations with unit tests
- [x] CI workflow and gating logic
- [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-1023, ENG-1107)
- [x] Docs updated with configuration options and troubleshooting
- [x] Verified non-blocking mode for release branches

Notes: The description includes the rationale and configuration examples in the docs. This PR intentionally keeps the per-PR run lightweight (~30s on typical prompt-set) by sampling evaluation inputs and running cached model variants when possible.

motivation_summary: Provide fast, deterministic PR-level feedback for prompt-set regressions by integrating lightweight metrics into eval-harness and gating them at CI to reduce regression latency and developer churn.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover metric edge cases (empty embeddings, identical prompts). PR-level CI uses sampled prompt fixtures (~50 examples) to keep runtime low. Staging run executed against a cached model snapshot to validate numeric stability. Manual verification steps included running the action locally against a feature branch and verifying GitHub comment formatting.
docs_changes: docs/eval-harness/ci-gating.md updated with configuration, examples, and migration notes. Short section added to docs/ops/alerts.md explaining how eval-gates map to incident thresholds.
alerts_and_rollouts: Gating enabled by default for main and feature branches. For release/* branches gating is configured as non-blocking (reports only). Monitoring: added a dashboard tile (eval.harness.prompt_gate.failures) and an alert that fires if more than 3 PR gates fail in 1 hour.
